ios.desc:
Checking your balance tells you what you have. Not what’s safe to spend.

Daily spending often feels uncertain. Lång makes it clear.

You already check your balance and try to pace your spending. Some days less, some days more. Adjusting by feel, trying to stay on track.

But everyday spending is irregular – quiet days, then everything at once. It’s hard to know what’s actually okay to spend today.

Lång gives you a daily safe spend amount. Stay within it most days and your money lasts. Spend less and build extra capacity. It adjusts when you overspend.

Enter what you feel you can spend until you next get paid. Log your day-to-day spending. See what’s safe to spend at any moment.

No categories. No monthly limits. No bank connections.

You already check your balance and pace your spending. Lång makes that approach work better.

See what you can spend today – get started in 30 seconds.

———

Subscription & privacy

• Lång offers a free trial, then requires a paid subscription to keep using the app.

• Subscriptions are auto-renewing and continue unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period.

• Billing, renewals, and cancellations are handled by Apple through your Apple ID in the Settings app.

• The free trial is available one time per Apple ID and converts automatically to a paid subscription unless cancelled before the trial ends.

• Lång is a spending guide – not financial, investment, tax, or legal advice.

• Your spending data stays on your device. We collect only anonymous usage data.

Read our Terms of use and Privacy policy for full details.

quotes.text:
I’ve been working on an app called Lång. A daily spending guide. It shows you what’s okay to spend based on how much needs to last how long.

For over a decade, I’ve thought about how most people seem to resist the advice about money. And also how all advice is based on the same idea: seeing where your money went and making monthly plans based on that.

I think people feel that this is a poor match for how money works. So they improvise. And because we tend to not discuss money with others, they improvise on their own. What this typically looks like is checking their balance and trying to pace things.

I’ve been trying to design the app around that. Providing support to what seems like a natural, instinctive approach to managing money.
